VERDICT (2026-09-28, closing the gap phase-456 W9 recorded) — DIVERGENCE / REFUSE-LOUD, which is the verdict this row carried before W9 and now carries for the same reason it did then: the CAPABILITY is on the dispatch client, and what remains different is the budget.

WHAT W9 LEFT OPEN, AND WHAT CLOSED IT. W9 split `rclcpp::Client<S>` into the DISPATCH client (which it now is) and the future-style `nros::PollClient<S>`, and two verbs could not come with the dispatch half: `nros_cpp_service_client_server_available(storage, out)` and `nros_cpp_service_client_wait_for_service(storage, executor, timeout_ms)` read an `RmwServiceClient` in CALLER storage, which an arena-owned client does not have. So this row said a porter holding a `Client<S>::SharedPtr` could not wait for a server at all, and named the remedy: those two entry points gaining the `(executor, handle_id)` arm the granted-QoS one has had since issue 1437.

That is exactly what landed, and nothing else did. `nros_cpp_service_client_server_available(storage, executor, handle_id, out)` and `nros_cpp_service_client_wait_for_service(storage, executor, handle_id, timeout_ms)` now take both roads — `storage` non-NULL for the owner, otherwise the arena index — so `rclcpp::Client<S>` and `nros::ClientHandle<S>` (what `Client<S>::SharedPtr` names) answer `wait_for_service` and `service_is_ready` on upstream's own argument list, with no member added to either type: `{executor_, handle_id_}` was already there for `async_send_request`. `nros::PollClient<S>` keeps passing its `storage_` and is unchanged in behaviour.

THE REFUSAL WAS NOT WEAKENED, and this is why the verdict is not `landed`-shaped. Upstream's signature is `template<typename RepT, typename RatioT> bool wait_for_service(std::chrono::duration<RepT, RatioT> timeout = duration(-1))`; ours is `Result wait_for_service(uint32_t timeout_ms)` with the no-argument form a `static_assert` carrying `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT`. The three differences the phase-417 statement below enumerates all stand, so the row stays `divergence` / `refuse-loud` with that statement as its subject.

WHAT WAS REFUSED, AGAIN. An `Executor&` parameter on the C++ signature would also have closed this, and was refused for the reason the (now closed) `cpp:Subscription::get_actual_qos` row refused it: a method whose whole purpose is to adopt upstream's spelling cannot close a gap by changing that spelling. Both halves of that pair are shut now, each by the same shape rather than by a new argument — the dispatch subscription carries its executor since phase-467 (2026-09-25, its row DELETED because nothing was left to say), this one carries its own.

ONE CONCEPT, THREE REFUSAL SITES. `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT` now fires from `nros::PollClient<S>`, `rclcpp::Client<S>` and `nros::ClientHandle<S>`, each with its OWN expected-failure TU on the `just check cpp` loop (`ros2_refuse_unbounded_wait_probe.cpp`, `..._dispatch_probe.cpp`, `..._handle_probe.cpp`) — phase-417's rule, because an expected-failure compile proves only that a file does not build, so refusals sharing a TU cannot be told apart and a half-fix reads as green. The POSITIVE half (the budgeted call on all three types) is in `rclcpp_node_freestanding_surface.cpp`, hosted and `-nostdinc++`, plus `ros2_api_adoption_stage2.cpp` for the ported hosted shape.

IN-TREE COST: zero, and unchanged from W9's statement — all five `wait_for_service` call sites create their client through the future-style road.

--- phase-456 W9 (2026-09-18), preserved: the gap as it was recorded ---

GAP, and it was OURS before: this row now records a capability that MOVED rather than one we never had.

`wait_for_service` and `service_is_ready` were both on `rclcpp::Client<S>` when that one class served two owners behind a `callback_mode_` flag. W9 split it, for the reason W2b and W5 split the subscription and the service: on the DISPATCH path the executor arena owns the client and `storage_` is never filled, so either call handed `NROS_SERVICE_CLIENT_SIZE` value-initialized zero bytes to an FFI whose own doc comment says `storage` must be "a valid initialized future-style service client", with `initialized_` true and nothing on the path checking.

After the split the FUTURE-STYLE half (`nros::PollClient<S>`) owns `storage_` and answers both unchanged — `cpp:PollClient::wait_for_service`, `cpp:PollClient::service_is_ready`. The DISPATCH half answered NEITHER, which is what the closure above fixed.

THE MEASURED REASON, and it was narrower than it looked. Of the four things issue 1437 and phase-444 put on this class, TWO reached the arena and two did not: `nros_cpp_service_client_get_actual_qos(storage, executor, handle_id, …)` had both roads by construction, so the granted-QoS pair answered on both halves with no weakening, and `get_service_name` reads a C++-side copy each half keeps. `nros_cpp_service_client_server_available` and `..._wait_for_service` had only the storage road. So the gap was exactly two verbs, and its cause was two FFI signatures rather than anything about the C++ shape — which is why closing it moved no C++ signature.

--- phase-417 stage 3, preserved ---

phase-417 stage 3 (2026-09-11) -- CLOSED as REFUSE-LOUD. The type difference was already the loud half; the DEFAULT was the live defect and it is gone.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `template<typename RepT, typename RatioT> bool wait_for_service(std::chrono::duration<RepT, RatioT> timeout = duration(-1))` -- the default is -1, BLOCK INDEFINITELY, and the return is a bare `bool`.

OURS: `Result wait_for_service(uint32_t timeout_ms)` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/client.hpp`). Three differences:
  * a ported `wait_for_service(1s)` is a COMPILE ERROR -- no `std::chrono` -> `uint32_t` conversion. Loud, correct under the rule, UNCHANGED.
  * `Result` rather than `bool` -- RFC-0018 forbids exceptions, so a timeout and a not-yet-initialised client must be distinguishable by return code. UNCHANGED.
  * the DEFAULT was 5000 ms. A ported no-argument `client->wait_for_service()` returned `Timeout` after five seconds where upstream was still waiting, and `[[nodiscard]]` does not catch `if (!client->wait_for_service())`, which is what upstream code actually writes. CLOSED: the default is gone and the no-argument form is a member template whose `static_assert` carries `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_WAIT`.

WHY REFUSE RATHER THAN ADOPT THE -1: the previous revision of this row said "nothing about a fixed arena forbids a blocking wait". That is true of the arena and wrong about the executor. `cpp:Client::wait_for_action_server` had already recorded the actual constraint, and it is RFC-0021: this helper drives the executor COOPERATIVELY while it probes, so a wait that never returns starves every other entity on a single-threaded transport. The budget is also unsigned, so there is no value to port -1 to. Given a bounded wait is the only thing this call offers, the rule says say so at the earliest knowable point -- refuse the un-timed call -- rather than substitute a budget the caller did not choose, which is exactly what the previous revision of this row proposed.

THE CLASS, not the site. `rclcpp_action::Client<A>::wait_for_action_server(uint32_t timeout_ms = 5000)` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_action/client.hpp`) had the identical defect against the identical upstream default, and is fixed in the same commit under the SAME message -- one refusal concept, two sites. Sweep: `grep -n '_ms = [0-9]' packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/*.hpp` enumerates every defaulted millisecond argument in the C++ API; the remaining ones (`Client::call`, `call_polling`, `Future::wait`'s `poll_ms`, `Executor::spin`/`spin_for`'s `poll_ms`, `Stream::wait_next`'s `poll_ms`) are OURS-ONLY verbs or cadence knobs with no upstream default to contradict, not instances of this class. `cpp:Client::wait_for_action_server`'s own row still reads `adopt-bounded` and says a ported argument-free call "compiles and does what it says"; that sentence is now false and the row needs re-verdicting to `refuse-loud`. It is left to its owner rather than edited here.

HELD BY: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_unbounded_wait_probe.cpp` and `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_unbounded_action_wait_probe.cpp` -- two TUs, not one, because an expected-failure compile proves only that a file does not build, so two refusals in one TU cannot be told apart and a half-fix would still read as green. Both are on the `just check cpp` refusal loop, which greps each failure for `REFUSED by nano-ros`. Negative control against the pre-fix headers: both COMPILED.

IN-TREE COST: zero. All five `wait_for_service` call sites and every `wait_for_action_server` call site already pass a budget.
